input:
limit as x tends to pi/2 of (cot x - cos x)/((pi - 2x)^3) equals

Options:
A. 1/24
B. 1/16
C. 1/8
D. 1/4

phase_1_understand_the_problem.problem_restatement: Evaluate a trigonometric limit at x -> pi/2 with cubic denominator.
phase_1_understand_the_problem.key_observation: Substitute x = pi/2 - h so denominator becomes (2h)^3 and use standard small-angle limits.

key_formulas.limits: lim_{h->0} sin h/h = 1, lim_{h->0} (sin h - h)/h^3 = -1/6

phase_3_plan_the_approach.strategy: Transform everything into h and reduce to known expansions for tan h and sin h.
logical_steps: Step 2: Rewrite numerator as tan h - sin h

step_1_substitute.transformed_limit: L = lim_{h->0} (tan h - sin h)/(2h)^3 = (1/8) lim_{h->0} (tan h - sin h)/h^3

step_2_expand.series: tan h = h + h^3/3 + O(h^5), sin h = h - h^3/6 + O(h^5)

phase_5_verify_answer.verification: Cubic terms dominate and yield coefficient 1/2 in numerator over 8 in denominator, giving 1/16.
